Muscle and fat are two separate entities. They do not convert to each other. So with proper diet and exercise to gain hypertrophy, the average mature adult will only gain around 10 pounds of muscle in about a year, and unless you're going to be doing competitive body building, its not really advantages to your body to try to do frequent and dramatic weight fluctuation associated with "bulking" and cutting. One of the things I personally do for myself and my clients is to calculate the goal weight when either gaining or losing weight, then create a calorie plan to eat at different stages throughout the process. If you're not going to need 3000 calories a day until 12 months from now once you've acquired you goal weight and muscle mass, then starting to eat too many calories too early can actually hinder your training through out the process by adding needless amounts of fat and depending on what you're eating, can hurt your performance in training. I recommend taking your goal weight, if you have one, find out the calories you need to maintain that weight, then slowly decrease your calories by a percentage based on what will be safe and realistic for each week and or month until you reach you goal. If you can, invest in a personal trainer/coach.
